samuel1.1.p1.b1.text: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim.

samuel1.1.p1.b2.text: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

samuel1.1.p1.b3.text: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh,

samuel1.1.p1.b4.text: where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.

samuel1.1.p2.b1.text: And whenever the day came for Elkanah to present his sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

samuel1.1.p2.b2.text: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.

samuel1.1.p2.b3.text: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her and taunt her viciously.

samuel1.1.p2.b4.text: Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunted her until she wept and would not eat.

samuel1.1.p3.b1.text: Hannah, why are you crying? … Why won’t you eat? Why is your heart so grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?

samuel1.1.p3.b2.text: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up.

samuel1.1.p3.b3.text: Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

samuel1.1.p4.b1.text: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.

samuel1.1.p4.b2.text: O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son,

samuel1.1.p4.b3.text: then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever come over his head.

samuel1.1.p5.b1.text: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.

samuel1.1.p5.b2.text: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk

samuel1.1.p5.b3.text: How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!

samuel1.1.p6.b1.text: No, my lord … I am a woman oppressed in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.

samuel1.1.p6.b2.text: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”

samuel1.1.p6.b3.text: Go in peace … and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.

samuel1.1.p7.b1.text: May your maidservant find favor with you

samuel1.1.p7.b2.text: Then she went on her way, and she began eating again, and her face was no longer downcast.

samuel1.1.p7.b3.text: The next morning Elkanah and Hannah got up early to bow in worship before the LORD, and then returned home to Ramah. … and the LORD remembered her.

samuel1.1.p7.b4.text: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel,

samuel1.1.p7.b5.text: Because I have asked for him from the LORD.

samuel1.1.p8.b1.text: After the boy is weaned … I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.

samuel1.1.p8.b2.text: Do what you think is best … Only may the LORD confirm His word.

samuel1.1.p8.b3.text: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.

samuel1.1.p8.b4.text: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.

samuel1.1.p9.b1.text: Please, my lord … as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.

samuel1.1.p9.b2.text: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,

samuel1.1.p9.b3.text: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.

samuel1.1.p9.b4.text: So they worshiped the LORD there.
